text: The shape of the field-capture decision entry and of its two reads is read as follows and is written in the story as a placeholder, never as a guess: the entry carries entryId, chainSeq, caseId, decisionCode, ruleId, ruleVersion, inputsRef, a recommendation holding the document type, the capture kind and the item result, finalCall, an object reference holding the document ID of a stored capture or the client file ID of a refused item, the client file ID, the document type code, the capture kind, the capture time, the message id of a refusal, decidedAt, prevHash, entryHash, correctsEntryId and actorUserId, as new columns of decision_log_entry; the DecisionLogPage answer carries items, page, size and total and is filterable by the object reference as well as by the eight query values of TSD P7 v2 T-A.2; the final call values are ACCEPTED, REFUSED and QUARANTINED, taken from the item result of the legacy field-capture response; MSG-P7-009 names ruleVersion or decisionCode and MSG-GEN-006 names the system that is unavailable; and the decision-log view of a case is described without a panel id.
why: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 has no column for a document, a client file, a type, a capture kind, a capture time or a message id, T-A.2 gives no answer field set and no object-reference filter, and the texts of MSG-P7-009 and MSG-GEN-006 are named but never written out; inventing any of them would put a value into the build that no owner approved.
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1, T3.2, T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD P7 v3 A2.1.4.2 AC-ALT-P7-001-02 and A2.2.4.3; legacy RWB-E2-024 sections 4, 11, 12 and 14; RWB-ITG-E2024-ITG sections 4, 7 and 12; ownership.json api rows GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId} to P7

impact: The entry, the two reads and the message set are built against the assumed shape; a later contract revision renames fields and messages without a change of behaviour, because the capture values themselves are rwb-document's and are only referenced here

text: The fail-closed rule of principle 5 applies to every governance action: when the decision record of a load, an approval, a promotion or a rollback cannot be written, the action is not committed, MSG-P7-003 is returned and an incident is raised. This extends FSD P7 VR-P7-001-2 and legacy BR8 from the match to the governance operations.
why: The sources state the rule for a decision and for the match, and the governance action is the same kind of record-bearing change.

confirm: P7 business analyst at the governance walkthrough
impact: If the registry may commit without its record, the transaction boundary and one exception path change; no criterion is lost

text: The append is one synchronous operation of rwb-decision on the decision base, POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log, called by rwb-agent as the first step of its feedback transaction with the case reference, the run reference, the item key SUMMARY, the verdict, the reason and an idempotency key of the run and the item, and answered 201 with the record reference, the chain sequence, the entry hash and the decided time; the record exists only when the answer returns, and a failure leaves rwb-agent's feedback unwritten. The per-service login is called the rwb-decision login (DP-02) because its name is not given, and the request and answer field set of section 12.1 stays the placeholder until the contract baseline is agreed.
why: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 documents only the two reads of the ledger and the legacy story writes the entry in process inside the monolith, so the write path of the target has neither a method nor a path nor a body, while rwb-agent has to store a decision reference on its feedback row and the whole action has to fail when the record cannot be written.

why: The legacy story calls D6 an assumed code and gives no LOV-DECISION values, and TSD P7 v2 T3.2 carries no decision code list at all, so a record cannot be validated or tested without a stated reading of where the values live and which values they are.

text: The reason of a correction or of a rejection is validated on its presence and its length of at most 1,000 characters and not against a code set, and the list of reason codes is left to the reference data of the verdict rather than written here; the record stores the reason as the override reason of the entry and the report of reason codes is not this story's.
why: The legacy story requires a reason and a monthly report of coded reasons and gives no code values, TSD P7 v2 carries no reason list, and a story may not invent business values to fill a validation it has no list for.

text: This story has no feature switch of its own: the legacy flag rwb.agent.intake-l1 stays with RWB-P10-E2028-APP, it gates the agent-output read and the panel there, and it never gates the append of the record, because a record that could be switched off would break REQ-DRI-005 and R-UNI-39; a verdict that arrives always writes its record.
why: The legacy story sets one flag for the whole capability and the target splits the capability across two services, so the flag has to be placed, and placing it on the record path would let a configuration change create an unrecorded decision.
